(c)
parts.text:
Tollens' reagent can be used to distinguish between aldehydes and ketones. Tollens' reagent contains $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]\text{OH}$, which can be prepared in a two-step process.

step 1 Aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ is added dropwise to aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ to form $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ as a brown precipitate.

step 2 Aqueous $\text{NH}_3$ is added dropwise to $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ to form a colourless solution containing $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]\text{OH}$.

Construct equations for each of the steps in the preparation of $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]\text{OH}$.

parts.text:
An electrochemical cell uses $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ as the positive electrode and $\text{Zn}$ as the negative electrode immersed in an alkaline electrolyte.

The overall cell reaction is shown.

$$\text{Ag}_2\text{O} + \text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Ag} + \text{Zn}(\text{OH})_2$$

Complete the half-equation for the reaction at each electrode.

$$\text{at the positive electrode} \quad \text{Ag}_2\text{O} + \ldots\ldots$$

$$\text{at the negative electrode Zn +} \ldots\ldots$$
